newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - July 21.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Fidel Ramos said the economy is on track as the peso steadily recovered over the last three days from its fall last week. (MANILA BULLETIN)

- President Ramos said doomsayers were wrong in predicting the Philippine economy will collapse as a result of the speculative attacks on the peso and the government's decision to float the currency. (TIMES JOURNAL)
- Defense Secretary Renato de Villa formally announced on Sunday that he would run for president in 1998 before a hometown crowd of 5,000 people led by President Ramos' men. (INQUIRER)
- Andrew Cunanan, the chameleon-like suspected serial killer of designer Gianni Versace and four other men, may now be masquerading as a woman, authorities said on Saturday (INQUIRER)

- Manila Mayor Alfredo Lim vowed to exhaust "all means" to rid the city of drug pushers and users despite allegations of civil rights obligations. Lim recently sparked an uproar for his unorthodox campaign of painting houses of alleged drug pushers with "Beware, drug pusher's house" or "Drug pusher lives here." (MALAYA)

- The united opposition party, the Laban ng Makabayang Masang Pilipino (LAMMP), sees the break-up of Lakas, the administration party, happening soon saying the seven Lakas presidential contenders are unlikely to stick to the party's selection process. (TODAY)
- The Philippines will draw a total of $712.3 million loan from the International Monetary Fund (IMF) to beef up the country's gross international reserves. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- The Board of Investments (BOI) has relaxed its debt-to-equity ratio requirement imposed on projects seeking government tax and fiscal incentives. Trade Undersecretary Melito Salazar said the BOI would not require a strict 75:25 debt-to-equity ratio in their project financing but a reasonable ratio. (ALL NEWSPAPERS)
- The Central Bank expects the peso to continue recovering this week even as it promised further cuts in its closely watched overnight borrowing rate. (TIMES/BUSINESSWORLD)

- The Central Bank predicted the peso-dollar exchange rate will settle to an average of 27 pesos to 28 pesos within the third quarter and would even hit its pre-speculative attack rate by the fourth quarter of this year. (CHRONICLE)

- Iran is pouring some $4 billion worth of investments in Mindanao for joint venture projects in oil refiney, liquefied petroleum gasoline depots, cement, steel and truck assembly plant, Trade Secretary Cesar Bautista said. (TIMES JOURNAL)
- Petron Corp said it may or may not increase prices of petroleum products this month, depending on the movement of the peso-dollar exchange rate this week. (MANILA STANDARD)
